case_title.reason: Header reads 'KRISHAN v. STATE OF HARYANA'; matches the case title.

number_of_accused.reason: Appeal decides liability of Krishan only; mother Shardi's acquittal was maintained.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is the husband who poured kerosene and is referred to as 'he'.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is stated.

accused_caste.reason: No caste of the accused is named; 'Balmiki' refers only to the victim.

accused_occupation.reason: No occupation of the accused is stated.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No wealth or class statement about the accused appears.

victim_caste.reason: PW14 autopsy record states 'Rani wife of Krishan Balmiki by Caste'.

victim_religion.reason: No religion of the victim is stated.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused is the victim's husband; spouse relationship is described.

offence_category.reason: Offence converted to s.302 after death; murder by burning is supported.

statutory_provisions.reason: Headnote lists ss.302, 498A, 109 r/w 34; FIR originally under s.307 is also noted.

weapon.reason: Accused poured kerosene oil on the victim and set her on fire.

evidence_type.reason: Dying declaration, post-mortem, SDJM/IO testimony and partly hostile witnesses are all discussed.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused; the dying declaration is the victim's statement.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Beatings under liquor and car-money demands are alleged in the dying declaration, as the value notes.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: Court notes no mitigating facts; the accused's attempt to extinguish the fire was a defence point only.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court acquitted both accused, finding the dying declaration not safe to rely upon.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court reversed acquittal of Krishan and maintained acquittal of Shardi.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, so the conviction stands.

offence_finally_established.reason: Murder by burning is supported; the judgment does not specify the convicted sections.

imprisonment_type.reason: The judgment refers to a sentence order but never states the sentence type.

imprisonment_years.reason: No fixed-term sentence is stated, so null is appropriate.

neutral_facts.correct_value: A summary of 150-300 words; the draft runs about 360 words.
neutral_facts.quote: The statement of the deceased was recorded on 30th March, 1998 at about 11.40 a.m.
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate and outcome-neutral, but the summary exceeds the 300-word limit and 'question-and-answer form' is not stated for this record.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the punishment prescribed for s.302.

attempt_completion.reason: Victim died from the burns, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death from burns of about 75%, ante-mortem and sufficient to cause death, is recorded.

number_of_offences.correct_value: 3 charged; finally upheld count not stated
number_of_offences.quote: prosecuted along-with another accused (his mother) ulss. 302, 498A and 109 r/w s. 34 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Three charged sections are supported, but the number of convictions upheld is not determinable from the judgment.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is involved.

premeditation_planning.reason: The court makes no finding of premeditation or planning.

motive.reason: Motive is marked as alleged in the dying declaration (car money demands and liquor-fuelled beatings), consistent with the judgment.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Dying declaration, PW14 post-mortem and partial support from named witnesses are accepted in paras 23-26.

witness_credibility.reason: Hostile witnesses held relevant but not decisive; doctor's thumb answer held no advantage to defence.

post_offence_conduct.reason: No post-offence conduct such as absconding or disclosure is noted.

trial_duration.reason: Trial judgment 15 Nov 1999, High Court 17 July 2007 and Supreme Court 13 Dec 2012 are given; offence date is not.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel for appellant and respondent are listed exactly as the judgment names them.

investigation_status.reason: FIR registration, amendment to s.302, site plan, inquest and post-mortem are all described.

procedural_irregularity.reason: The court notes no procedural lapse; its criticism concerns the trial judge's appreciation of evidence.

appeal_history.reason: Trial acquittal, High Court conviction of Krishan and Supreme Court dismissal are accurately listed.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State argued the dying declaration need not be corroborated if true, relying on Ram Sagar Yadav; the hostility point was the defence's submission.
prosecution_argument.quote: the counsel appearing for the State relied upon the judgment of this Court in the case of State of Uttar Pradesh v. Ram Sagar Yadav
prosecution_argument.reason: The State's Ram Sagar Yadav argument is correct, but the hostility-of-witnesses argument was raised by the defence (para 22).

defence_argument.reason: Khushal Rao corroboration point, doctor's thumb answer and hostile-witness submission are all made by the appellant's counsel.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Court applied the rule that a true, reliable dying declaration can be sole basis; hostility is relevant but not determinative.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: All six cases and citations match those the judgment relies on.

sentencing_rationale.reason: No sentence rationale is given, so 'Not applicable' fits.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The court weighed no mitigating factors.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The court weighed no aggravating factors in sentencing terms.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or other orders are given.
